input.rationale: Section 7 contains only a mutual waiver of consequential/indirect damages (carved out for indemnification and confidentiality) and no monetary cap; searches for \"aggregate liability\", \"exceed\" and \"liable\" return no cap language anywhere in the Agreement, and Section 5 is a revenue-share with no Customer-paid fees. The clause therefore fails the fallback (mutual cap of 12 months' fees with carve-outs) on a material term — no cap exists at all, leaving both parties, including AP, with unlimited direct-damages exposure. Redline inserts a mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable between the Parties and USD 1,000,000, with uncapped Excluded Claims (confidentiality/data protection/security, indemnification, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud, IP infringement) aligned to the existing Section 7(a) carve-outs, and confirms Kubient's Section 5 revenue-share payment obligations sit outside the cap.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual aggregate liability cap with standard uncapped carve-outs to Section 7.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 excludes consequential damages but sets no monetary cap, so both parties carry unlimited direct-damages exposure. We have added our standard mutual cap at the greater of twelve months' amounts paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality/data security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement sitting outside the cap, consistent with the existing carve-outs in Section 7(a). We can discuss a straight twelve-month cap if the fixed floor is an issue.

ops.text: EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (I) THE AMOUNTS PAID OR PAYABLE BETWEEN THE PARTIES UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (II) USD 1,000,000. "Excluded Claims" means a Party's breach of its confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, willful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights. Amounts payable by Kubient to Customer under Section 5 are not subject to this limitation.
